claims.text: Tailored thermomechanical processing can refine an inherited eutectic lamellar structure into an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure.
This microstructural refinement can simultaneously improve the strength–ductility synergy of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Conventionally cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a coarse lamellar or conventional eutectic microstructure.
A sequence of cold rolling or comparable deformation followed by controlled annealing produces the proposed ultrafine-grained duplex lamellar architecture.
Phase decomposition occurs during formation of the processed hierarchical microstructure.
Controlled recrystallization is required for the intervention to work.
The processed material forms a hierarchical duplex microstructure that inherits the eutectic lamellae.
The inherited hierarchical lamellae generate a two-hierarchical constraint effect.
The processed microstructure generates microcrack-arresting features or behavior.
The inherited lamellar duplex structure acts as an in situ composite.
Ultrafine grains increase strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
The duplex architecture promotes deformation twinning that enhances ductility.
The two-hierarchical constraint effect and self-generated microcrack arrest improve the mechanical response during deformation.
Relative to conventionally cast material, thermomechanically processed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will have higher yield strength and higher ductility.
Yield strength and ductility will each increase by approximately 20% or more relative to the cast baseline.
The intervention should also work in other eutectic high-entropy alloys with composition and phase stability similar to AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The intervention may be ineffective when alloy composition or phase stability prevents formation of the duplex microstructure.
